lines.text: Today you organise data like a real app, from a whole cricket team to your own virtual pet.
A list can hold dictionaries, one for each player. team[0]["runs"] means the runs of the first player.
This is how real apps store tables of data.
for player in team: gives you one dictionary at a time.
You can read it, add it up or change it, like player["runs"] += 4.
Every record has the same keys.
class Pet: describes what every pet has and what it can do.
Pet("Moti") builds one real pet object from the blueprint.
You can build as many pets as you like.
Inside the class, self means this particular pet. self.hunger = 5 is an attribute, a value the pet remembers. def feed(self): is a method, an action you call with pet.feed().
Each player is a dictionary with the same keys, and the list holds them all.
Team zero name means the first record, then its name key.
We start by guessing that the first player is the best.
Whenever we find someone with more runs, they become the new best.
The init method runs every time we build a new pet from the blueprint.
Moti and Bijli are two separate objects, and each remembers its own name.
A method is a function that lives inside the class and always starts with self.
When we call moti dot feed, self means Moti, so only Moti gets less hungry.
Python always passes the object itself into a method, as the first argument.
The method forgot to accept it. Writing self in the brackets fixes the error.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
